newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Global 96 flows to emerging markets put at $50 bln.
newsitem.headline: Global 96 flows to emerging markets put at $50 bln.

text.p: An estimated $50 billion of world money went into emerging markets in 1996 after a disappointing $15 billion in 1995, and the recovery should continue in 1997, Michael Howell, head of London's Crossborder Capital, said.
He told an international investment conference in Geneva on Tuesday that annual cash flows into emerging markets were still below 1993's peak of $63 billion during a global rush.
But the duration of the recovery should be longer, he said.

Howell said he believed emerging markets will be buoyed in 1997 by a wave of international liquidity flowing from the developed markets as well as prospects of lower interest rates and high domestic liquidity.
"In 1997, I will be switching out of East Europe and moving into South Europe," said Howell, adding he saw signs of the beginning of overheating in East Europe.
His favourite emerging market picks for 1997 were Mauritius, Chile, India, Philippines, Greece, Indonesia, South Korea, Mexico, Turkey and Pakistan.
